Theorem
[Solution of the Euler--Lagrange equation] ↗ def:weak-solution-euler-lagrange-scalar 1. ch8:8.2-thm-4\group Existence of Minimizers

Assume $L$ verifies the growth conditions (35), (36), and $u \in \mathcal{A}$ satisfies \[ I[u] = \min _{w \in \mathcal{A}} I[w]. \] Then $u$ is a weak solution of (37).

Proof

\sketch For $v\in W_0^{1,q}(U)$, differentiate $I[u+\tau v]$ at zero. The growth bounds justify differentiation under the integral, and minimality forces the resulting weak Euler–Lagrange identity to vanish.

□
